page: Google Cloud Platform e2-micro is an entry-level instance within the E2 family designed for minimal workloads. It features an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz, providing 2 vCPUs powered by a shared physical core with 1/8 allocation and hyper-threading enabled. The system includes 1.0 GB of system memory, yielding 0.5 GB per vCPU. Cache architecture consists of 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. It supports x86_64 CPU instructions including AVX, AES encryption acceleration, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, but lacks AVX-512 extensions. The instance has no attached local NVMe storage and includes no dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results place the e2-micro in the bottom 10 percent across tested performance categories. Single-core and multi-core CPU testing via stress-ng yields scores of 132.9 and 171.0 respectively. PassMark CPU testing produces an overall CPU score of 201.56, with extended instructions scoring 138.59 and encryption scoring 76.5. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 0.1 GB/sec, while write bandwidth reaches 1.33 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates a Redis SET throughput of 0.2 million operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 0.17 GB/sec.

Given the shared CPU allocation and low memory capacity, the e2-micro delivers high cost efficiency for lightweight background tasks where compute demands are minimal and intermittent. The key hardware tradeoff is restricted compute capacity and low memory bandwidth, which severely limits execution speed under sustained processing loads. Recommended workload fits include low-traffic web servers, basic microservices, lightweight administrative scripts, cron jobs, and development or testing environments.

The processor includes 16 MB L3 cache and supports AVX, AES, and FMA instruction sets. The instance lacks local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmark performance consistently falls in the bottom 10 percent of cloud instances, recording a stress-ng multi-core score of 171.0, a PassMark CPU score of 201.56, and static web serving throughput of 0.17 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 0.1 GB/sec. Due to shared vCPU capacity, the e2-micro provides a cost-effective platform for low-utilization tasks, including lightweight microservices, internal administrative tools, small development environments, and automated background scripts.
